subject: Post-call: evaluation calibration + live test plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <m.lopez@vertexhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T14:08:00-05:00
Subject: Quick recap + next steps (evaluation calibration + live test)

Marta — thanks again for the time today. I wanted to capture the key points from our call and propose a short test plan so we keep momentum heading into procurement. If I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Fragmented inference performance across teams, spiky latency during peak batch jobs, and rising token costs with current provider.
- Goal: Standardize inference to reduce 95th percentile latency below 200ms for our customer-facing endpoints, and cut per-token cost by ~25% while preserving generation quality.
- Constraints: PHI-sensitive workloads for Q1 pilots; Vertex needs SOC2 evidence and an SLA with a 2xx% availability target included in procurement.

Decision criteria we heard
1) Latency consistency (95p latency)
2) Cost per 1k tokens at target throughput
3) Integration effort with existing API surface (minimal SDK changes)
4) Security/compliance (SOC2 evidence, VPC option)
5) Fallback/availability model during capacity events

Proposed short evaluation plan (two-week window)
- Week 1: Calibration tests — run identical prompt workloads across our hosted Redwood endpoint and your incumbent for a 24-hour steady-state and one 4-hour spike. We’ll provide the script and scorecard.
- Week 2: Live pilot — route 10% of production traffic for a 48-hour window to measure real-world latency, cost, and quality regressions.

Open questions (for procurement & infra)
- Can Vertex provide a small set of representative prompts and expected token distribution by Monday?
- Will procurement accept a 30-day pilot contract with a fixed cap for cost protection?

Attachments: I’ve attached a draft scorecard and an SLA summary for your legal team to skim.

Next actions
- Marta: confirm pilot window and whether procurement needs an MSA redline before the pilot (reply by EOD Tue).
- Marissa & Ben: prep calibration script + scorecard and a brief runbook for your infra team.
- I’ll schedule the kickoff call and include procurement/legal if you want them on the first sync.

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments (referenced): redwood-eval-scorecard-v1.xlsx, redwood-sla-summary.pdf

Sean — appreciate the clear summary. Quick answers:
- We can provide a sample set of 300 prompts that represent the majority of our workflows (mix of short/long). Expect that by Monday 11/23 COB.
- Procurement is fine with a time-boxed 30-day pilot but will push for a capped spend commitment for internal approvals; I’ll send the cap range in the procurement note.

Marta

Subject: Internal: candidate comparison notes (post-call)

Quick internal summary after Marta’s replies — pulling this into the scorecard before we send it over. Key points for the bake-off matrix:
- Weighting suggestion (proposed): Latency consistency 30%, Cost 25%, Integration effort 15%, Security/compliance 20%, Fallback/availability 10%.
- Shortlist competitors they explicitly mentioned on the call: Incumbent A (managed), Vendor B (self-hosted partner). We should call out where Redwood’s autoscaling & prefix caching move the needle on cost/latency for their workload.
- Open technical clarifications we need from Vertex: expected concurrency distribution during their 4-hour spike, and any hard limits on token retention (KV cache retention policy).

Action items for us (Marissa): attach the runbook + preliminary scorecard and include test harness instructions (JMeter + Python wrapper). Ben — can you validate that the runbook covers the VPC pilot steps? If yes, I’ll attach and send to Marta.

—Marissa

- Pilot cap: understood. We’ll propose a pilot spend cap with a safety buffer and include that in the pilot agreement.
- Security: looping in our security checklist (attached). If InfoSec needs a call, Marissa can join and bring engineering for kernel-level questions.

Proposed kickoff calendar options (pick one):

- Thu 11/25 11:00 AM ET — 30 min

Please confirm preferred kickoff time and whether procurement wants a short MSA redline before the pilot.
